title: The State’s own figures on coverage by immigration status
question: What do the State’s budget documents say State-only coverage, its repayments to Washington and the 2025 cuts cost or save?
finding: The November 2025 estimate added $819.3 million of General Fund in 2025-26 for State-only claiming adjustments for members with unsatisfactory immigration status, and $617.6 million for federal deferrals. It counts $66.4 million of recoupments on claims for these members, spread over three years, and cuts administrative claims by about $600.0 million a year from now on. The repayment of past federal claims (policy change 2415) is $397.7 million in 2025-26 in November and $686.6 million in May. Budget Act savings: Enrolment freeze, adults 19 and older without satisfactory status (from 1 Jan 2026), $77.9 million in 2025-26 and $3.30 billion in 2028-29; $30 monthly premiums, adults 19 to 59 with unsatisfactory status (from 1 Jul 2027), $695.7 million in 2027-28; End of clinic visit rates for State-only services (from 1 Jul 2026), $1.00 billion in 2026-27 and $1.10 billion in 2027-28; End of State-only dental cover, adults 19 and older (from 1 Jul 2026), $308.0 million in 2026-27 and $336.0 million in 2028-29; Drug rebate aggregator for State-only drug claims, $370.0 million in 2025-26 and $600.0 million in ongoing. Between November and May the State’s 2026-27 figures lost $1.58 billion of savings: Drug rebate aggregator (rebates for State-only drug claims), $435.0 million in November and nothing in May; End of clinic visit rates for State-only services (marked “DELETED” in the May estimate), $1.01 billion in November and nothing in May; End of dental cover for adults with unsatisfactory immigration status (marked “DELETED” in the May estimate), $134.6 million in November and nothing in May. Neither estimate gives one total for the cost of State-only coverage; the Legislative Analyst’s figure in the existing case remains the only total on disk.
how: Rows are the General Fund and total-fund amounts of each policy change that concerns coverage by immigration status, from the “current year compared to budget year” tables of both estimates, and the savings stated in the 2025-26 Budget Act highlights. A negative figure is a saving. The policy-change titles are shortened into plain words.
limits: Budget estimates are forecasts and change between editions. A policy change prices one change, not the whole program. The estimates do not break costs out by county, so no San Francisco figure can be made from them.
